summary:
The United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 and its 2025 single-sex-services code do not automatically extend to Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha; local law governs, and the United Kingdom measures can be applied only by Order in Council.

Consensual same-sex activity has been lawful in the territory since 2001, and the age of consent is equalised at 16 across all three island groups. The 2009 constitutional order imposed by the United Kingdom bans discrimination on grounds including sexual orientation territory-wide, and those protections have been in force since 2009.

Same-sex marriage was legislated island by island. The Ascension Island Council approved the marriage ordinance on 31 May 2016 by 5 votes to 0, it was signed and gazetted on 20 June 2016, and it commenced on 1 January 2017. Tristan da Cunha followed on 4 August 2017 and Saint Helena on 20 December 2017. Adoption by same-sex couples became lawful the same year.

The sources in this inventory are aggregator and index pages covering LGBT rights generally; none addresses gender recognition, identity documents, entry screening, or healthcare access for trans visitors.
tangentialFactors:
Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha is an Overseas Country or Territory of the European Union, and the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights is recorded as applicable there. That layer sits alongside local legislation and the United Kingdom constitutional framework, and does not by itself govern how a trans visitor is treated at the border or in a clinic.

The territory's three island groups legislate separately, so equality measures took effect on different dates in different places rather than through a single national instrument. The scale of the electorates is small enough that individual council votes are recorded in detail, as with the 5-0 Ascension result.
localsOnly:
Residents of all three island groups are covered by the anti-discrimination protections in force since 2009, which include sexual orientation as a protected ground, and by the equalised age of consent of 16.

Residents can enter same-sex marriages under ordinances that commenced on 1 January 2017 on Ascension Island, 4 August 2017 on Tristan da Cunha and 20 December 2017 on Saint Helena, and adoption has been available since 2017.

Legislation reaches residents through the individual island councils and the territorial framework rather than through the United Kingdom Parliament; the Ascension marriage ordinance moved through council approval, signature and gazettal, then commencement.
outOfScopeNotes:
No source in this inventory addresses legal gender recognition, the rules for changing sex or gender markers on passports or local identity documents, or what a trans visitor's documents must show on arrival. Those points remain unresolved here.

Enforcement of the 2009 anti-discrimination protections, any hate-crime provisions, complaints outcomes and the experience of trans people in policing, healthcare or single-sex facilities are not sourced. Nothing is stated about whether screening at entry could disclose a traveller's trans status.

The source base consists of aggregator pages: an Alchetron page updated 25 April 2026, Wikiwand mirrors of Wikipedia articles, and a GayLawNet index last accessed 23 June 2013 that cites ILGA's State-sponsored Homophobia. The GayLawNet entry may lag current law, and the aggregator pages are not primary legal texts; the ordinances and the 2009 constitutional order themselves were not consulted for this record.
